description:
FOUND s514 (Fable, 2026-10-10 12:41) by the s513g merge-review probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s513/review/p513g/fpath.pl (perl -> base cc3caca6 -> tree 499ffad6; make_path / mkpath / remove_tree / wrap / fill rows all = perl).  DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT TAKEN (lstat.pl, same dir): `lstat` returns an empty list with  set, `-e/-l/-d` are undef, `-d _ / -f _` after the failed lstat are undef, `unlink` returns 0 with ENOENT, `chmod` returns 0 -- all IDENTICAL to perl.  So the branch File::Path takes is wrong for another reason: in perl, _rmtree does `my (, , ) = (lstat )[0,1,2] or next ROOT_DIR;` -- a LIST SLICE of an EMPTY list in list assignment: perl's `(lstat )[0,1,2]` of an empty list is an EMPTY list, so the assignment yields 0 elements -> `or next` fires.  SUSPECT: PCL's list slice of an empty list yields (undef, undef, undef) (3 elements) so the assignment is true and the walk continues into the unlink branch.  Cheap probe: `my  = (); my (,,) = ()[0,1,2] or print "next\n"; print scalar(() = ()[0,1,2]), "\n"` -- perl prints `next` and 0.  If confirmed, this is a core list-slice rule (perlop: a slice of an empty list is empty) -- a runtime fix with a Pl/t row, and File::Path needs nothing.

CONFIRMED s514 (Fable, 2026-10-10 12:42; probe through probe.sh, perl 5.40.3 vs main 663b4d0b):
    my @e = ();
    my ($a, $b, $c) = (@e)[0,1,2] or print "next fired\n";          # perl: next fired   PCL: (silent)
    print scalar(() = (@e)[0,1,2]);                                     # perl 0             PCL 3
    my @s = (lstat("/nonexistent"))[0,1,2]; print scalar @s;         # perl 0             PCL 3
    my @one = (5); my @t = (@one)[0,1,2]; print scalar @t;          # perl 3             PCL 3  (out-of-range indexes of a NON-empty list DO yield undefs -- perlop)
The rule (perlop, Slices): "A slice of an empty list is still an empty list" -- only when the list is EMPTY; a slice with out-of-range indexes of a non-empty list yields undef per index.  FIX: the list-slice runtime op (grep the emission of `(LIST)[...]` -- p-list-slice or its family in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) returns the empty list when its source list has no elements, before indexing.  Guard: the four rows above in an existing Pl/t slice file (`Pl/t/slice-01.t` has a List Slices section) -- perl-oracle rows; inverse-verified.  This is a one-arm runtime fix for the next correctness batch; File::Path needs nothing (its `(lstat $root)[0,1,2] or next ROOT_DIR` then behaves).  Supersedes the suspect wording above.
subject: SILENT WRONG (core, CONFIRMED s514): a LIST SLICE of an EMPTY list yields N undefs in PCL where perl yields an EMPTY list -- `my ($a,$b,$c) = (@e)[0,1,2] or next` never fires, `scalar(() = (@e)[0,1,2])` is 3 (perl 0), `(lstat $missing)[0,1,2]` has 3 elements (perl 0); this is why File::Path::rmtree of a missing path warns twice (perl silent)
